question.text: A UNIQUE feature of Cat III AIFs (versus Cat I and Cat II) is that Cat III can be structured as:

answer.text: Perpetual with no maturity in any form

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI (AIF) Regulations, Cat I and Cat II MUST be close-ended. Only Cat III has the option to be either open-ended OR close-ended. This is a defining feature of Cat III — it allows daily/periodic NAV-based subscriptions and redemptions like a hedge fund. The Trap: Cat I/II ARE close-ended only — that's a Cat I/II-specific rule tested in XIX-A/D. Cat III is the unique open-ended-permitted category. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A and XIX-D test the Cat I/II close-ended-only rule. XIX-E tests the Cat III flexibility. Don't confuse the two! Manager's Pro-Tip: As a Cat III manager, choose open-ended for a daily-NAV liquid strategy (long-short, stat-arb) and close-ended for a strategy with illiquid exposure (event-driven with distressed sleeves). Match structure to liquidity.
